questions.q: What is the core structural difference between a Lakehouse and a Warehouse in Fabric?
options: A Lakehouse is schema-on-read and flexible; a Warehouse is a T-SQL engine that enforces a defined schema
A Lakehouse only stores files; a Warehouse only stores tables
A Warehouse cannot be queried with SQL at all
There is no structural difference — they are the same item type under a different name
questions.explain: A Lakehouse stores files and tables together and applies structure at query time (schema-on-read). A Warehouse is a full T-SQL engine with an enforced, defined schema (schema-on-write).

questions.q: Why might a governance-minded team steer BI-facing, reporting data toward a Warehouse instead of a Lakehouse?
options: A Warehouse guarantees a consistent, enforced structure that won't silently change shape under a report
A Warehouse is the only item type that can connect to OneLake
A Warehouse has no governance features at all
A Lakehouse cannot be read by Power BI
questions.explain: The lesson's governance decision is about the consumer: a Warehouse's enforced schema is the guaranteed contract that BI and reporting consumers need.

questions.q: Where do both a Lakehouse's and a Warehouse's actual data physically land, by default?
options: OneLake
A separate database server outside Fabric
Local disk on the user's machine
Azure Blob Storage, entirely unrelated to Fabric
questions.explain: Both item types are OneLake-backed — their actual data is stored in OneLake, the shared tenant-wide lake covered in Lesson 6.

questions.q: What roles does a newly created Lakehouse or Warehouse have by default, before any extra security is added?
options: It inherits the roles already assigned to the workspace it lives in
It starts with no access for anyone, including the creator
It automatically grants Admin to the entire organization
It requires a brand-new, separate role system unrelated to the workspace
questions.explain: Both item types inherit the workspace's existing roles (Admin/Member/Contributor/Viewer from Lesson 5) unless additional item-level OneLake security is layered on top, which Lesson 8 covers next.

questions.q: Where do Lakehouse and Warehouse both get created from in the Fabric UI?
options: The same "New item" picker
Two completely separate Fabric products that don't share a creation flow
Only through the admin portal's tenant settings
Only through a PowerShell script — there is no UI option
questions.explain: Both item types appear as cards in the same workspace "New item" picker, alongside other storage item types.
